tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.name: Caramelized Shrimp and Pork Belly
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.serving_basis: Four portions as the savory protein in a family meal with rice and vegetables.
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.description: Sweet shrimp and layered pork belly are cooked together in a lightly caramelized fish-sauce glaze. Serve with rice, greens and a mild soup for an everyday meal.
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.finished_dish: The shrimp are coral-colored and just firm, while the pork is tender with lightly browned edges and a thin glossy sauce.
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, cucumber or boiled greens, and a light soup.
tips: Pat the shrimp dry to keep the pan sauce from becoming watery.
Add the shrimp after the pork has softened and cook only until opaque and done.
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.image_alt: Caramelized shrimp and pork belly with scallions on a white ceramic plate.
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.time_note: About 55 minutes including a 10-minute marinade; add shrimp near the end so they stay tender.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Remove whiskers and devein if needed; rinse briefly and pat dry.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Choose a balanced lean-and-fat piece and slice into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and final seasoning.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use less if the pork renders a lot of fat.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use to soften the pork before adding shrimp.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Finish the dish with pepper.

ingredients.name: Chili powder
ingredients.notes: Optional; omit for a mild dish.

preparation_steps: Rinse and drain the shrimp; slice the pork belly and mince the garlic and shallot.
Season the pork with part of the fish sauce, sugar and pepper. Rest for about 10 minutes, then mix the remaining fish sauce with water.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and briefly saute the shallot and garlic. Add the pork and cook until firm and lightly browned.
Pour in the seasoned water, cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 10–12 minutes. Uncover and add the shrimp.
Cook until the shrimp turn coral and opaque and the sauce lightly coats the ingredients. Taste, finish with pepper and serve.
tom-rang-thit-ba-chi.media_alt_text: Orange-pink shrimp braised with glossy pork belly pieces on a white ceramic plate.

ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.name: Steamed Pomfret with Soy Sauce
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.serving_basis: One steamed pomfret, divided into four portions and served with rice and vegetables.
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.description: Whole pomfret is steamed with ginger and scallion, then dressed with a light soy-based sauce. This low-oil fish dish keeps the fish's natural sweetness for a family meal.
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.finished_dish: Opaque, tender fish flakes easily from the bone; ginger, scallion and soy are fragrant without overpowering the fish.
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled or stir-fried greens.
tips: Score the thickest part so the fish seasons and cooks evenly.
Start steaming only after the water is boiling; timing depends on fish size and thickness.
Check that the flesh near the backbone is opaque and separates easily before serving.
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.image_alt: Whole soy-steamed pomfret on a white platter with ginger strips and scallions.
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.time_note: About 65 minutes including 20 minutes of marinating; steam for 15–20 minutes depending on the fish.

ingredients.name: Pomfret
ingredients.notes: Clean, remove gills and innards, and score both sides.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly and use as a bed for the fish.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice some and cut the rest into fine strips.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into lengths; reserve a little for garnish.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Slice; optional.

ingredients.name: Light soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a moderately salty variety.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Adds a mild savory note.

ingredients.name: Sesame oil
ingredients.notes: Whisk into the sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use to briefly fry aromatics.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Whisk with the soy sauce.

preparation_steps: Rub the fish with a little salt, rinse and pat dry. Score the thickest part; slice the aromatics and mince the shallot and garlic.
Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar and water. Coat the fish and let it stand for about 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Arrange onion and several ginger slices in a deep plate, place the fish on top and steam over boiling water for about 15 minutes.
Add scallions, ginger strips and chili. Spoon the plate sauce over the fish and continue steaming until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Briefly fry the shallot and garlic in hot oil and spoon over the fish. Serve with some of the steaming liquid.
ca-chim-hap-xi-dau.media_alt_text: A whole steamed pomfret with soy sauce, shredded ginger and scallions on a ceramic platter.

cha-trung-hap.name: Vietnamese Steamed Egg and Pork Loaf
aliases: Steamed Egg Loaf for Broken Rice
cha-trung-hap.serving_basis: One steamed loaf cut into four portions; serve with broken rice or a home meal.
cha-trung-hap.description: Ground pork is mixed with eggs, glass noodles and wood-ear mushrooms, then steamed until tender. A thin egg-yolk topping gives the loaf its familiar golden surface; it is commonly served with Saigon broken rice.
cha-trung-hap.finished_dish: The loaf is set but moist, with strands of noodles and wood-ear mushroom inside and a thin golden top.
cha-trung-hap.serving: Slice while warm; pair with broken rice, pickled vegetables and fish-sauce dressing, or serve with steamed rice.
tips: Soak the glass noodles only until pliable and drain well so the mixture does not turn loose.
Do not pack the mixture tightly in the mold; steam needs to circulate.
Cover the mold to prevent condensation from dripping onto the surface, and steam until the center is fully set.
cha-trung-hap.image_alt: Steamed Vietnamese egg and pork loaf with a golden top, sliced to show noodles and wood-ear mushroom.
cha-trung-hap.time_note: About 65 minutes including 10 minutes to soak noodles and mushrooms; steam until the center is fully set.

ingredients.name: Ground lean pork
ingredients.notes: Choose pork with a little fat so the loaf stays moist.

ingredients.name: Chicken eggs
ingredients.notes: Reserve one yolk to brush over the surface.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Finely chop; optional if unavailable.

ingredients.name: Dried wood-ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Rehydrate, rinse thoroughly and chop.

ingredients.name: Dried glass noodles
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, drain and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season moderately.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the savory seasoning.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Adds fragrance.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Lightly grease the steaming mold.

preparation_steps: Soak the glass noodles in cool water until pliable, drain and cut short. Rehydrate the wood-ear mushrooms, rinse and chop; mince the straw mushrooms, shallot and scallions.
Separate one egg yolk. Beat the remaining eggs and the separated egg white in a bowl.
cooking_steps: Combine the ground pork with the eggs, noodles, mushrooms, shallot, scallion, fish sauce, sugar and pepper until evenly mixed.
Lightly oil a heatproof mold and spread the mixture evenly. Place it in a steamer over boiling water, cover and steam for about 20 minutes.
Brush the reserved yolk across the top and steam for another 8–10 minutes, until the surface sets and the center is fully cooked. Rest briefly before slicing.
cha-trung-hap.media_alt_text: Golden steamed egg loaf sliced to show glass noodles and wood-ear mushrooms, arranged on a white plate.

ga-hap-hanh.name: Vietnamese Steamed Chicken with Scallions
aliases: Steamed Chicken with Ginger and Scallions
ga-hap-hanh.serving_basis: About one kilogram of steamed chicken, divided among four people with rice and dipping salt.
ga-hap-hanh.description: Chicken is steamed over lemongrass, with ginger and mushrooms added during cooking and scallions placed on top near the end. The method keeps the meat moist and brings gentle aromatic flavor to a family meal.
ga-hap-hanh.finished_dish: The chicken is pale golden and moist, cooked through to the bone; scallions, ginger and mushrooms remain fragrant and tender.
ga-hap-hanh.serving: Chop into serving pieces and serve hot with lime-pepper salt or ginger fish sauce and steamed rice.
tips: Drain the chicken after rinsing and score thicker pieces so the seasoning reaches the meat.
Add the scallions near the end to keep their color and aroma.
Steaming time varies by piece size; check that the meat near the bone is fully cooked.
ga-hap-hanh.image_alt: Vietnamese steamed chicken pieces with fresh scallions and ginger on a white platter.
ga-hap-hanh.time_note: About 75 minutes including a 15-minute marinade; steam in stages until chicken is cooked through.

ingredients.name: Cut chicken
ingredients.notes: Use bone-in thighs or half a chicken cut into large pieces.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into lengths; reserve tender green tops.

ingredients.name: Fresh shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Rinse quickly and trim tough stems; rehydrated dried shiitake can be used instead.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise and cut into lengths.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice some and cut the rest into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little to clean and season the chicken.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Season lightly.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the chicken.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Pour into the steamer; keep it below the chicken plate.

preparation_steps: Rub the chicken with a little salt, rinse several times and drain. Score thicker pieces and season with salt, sugar, seasoning powder and pepper for about 15 minutes.
Rinse the lemongrass, ginger, scallions and mushrooms. Bruise the lemongrass, slice the ginger and cut the scallions into lengths.
cooking_steps: Bring the water in a steamer to a boil. Spread lemongrass in the basket, arrange the chicken in one layer and steam over medium heat for about 15 minutes.
Add ginger and shiitake mushrooms, cover and steam for another 10–15 minutes. Check the thickest piece; if it remains pink or the juices are cloudy, continue steaming.
Scatter scallions over the top and steam for about 5 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked. Serve hot with a dipping sauce of choice.
ga-hap-hanh.media_alt_text: Pale golden steamed chicken pieces with green scallions and shredded ginger on a ceramic plate.

bo-xao-dau-que.name: Vietnamese Beef Stir-Fried with Green Beans
bo-xao-dau-que.serving_basis: Four portions of beef and green beans for a family meal with rice and soup.
bo-xao-dau-que.description: Thinly sliced beef is quickly seared, then tossed with just-tender green beans. The dish pairs the sweetness of beef with crisp beans for a practical weekday meal.
bo-xao-dau-que.finished_dish: Tender beef with bright green beans, lightly coated in garlic sauce.
bo-xao-dau-que.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a mild soup.
tips: Slice the beef across the grain and stir-fry over high heat so it does not release too much liquid.
Blanch the green beans briefly to preserve color and reduce the stir-frying time.
Cook the beef separately and return it at the end so it stays tender.
search_terms: Vietnamese beef and green bean stir-fry
bo-xao-dau-que.image_alt: Beef stir-fried with bright green beans and garlic on a white plate.
bo-xao-dau-que.time_note: About 47 minutes including a 15-minute marinade; blanch the beans and cook the beef separately to keep both tender.

ingredients.name: Beef
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly across the grain so it cooks quickly and stays tender.

ingredients.name: Green beans
ingredients.notes: Trim the strings, rinse and cut into serving lengths.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Light soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use to season the beef and finish the dish.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly so it does not overpower the beans.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Divide between the beef and the beans.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually while stir-frying the beans.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly and adjust for the soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional, to balance the savory flavor.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Finish before serving.

preparation_steps: Trim and rinse the green beans, cut into short lengths and blanch in lightly salted boiling water for about one minute. Drain well.
Slice the beef thinly across the grain, slice the onion and mince the garlic. Marinate the beef with part of the soy sauce, oyster sauce and pepper for about 15 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat a little oil in a pan. Stir-fry the beef over high heat until just browned, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, briefly saute the garlic and onion, then add the green beans. Add a little water and seasoning, cover briefly and cook until the beans are tender-crisp.
Return the beef to the pan and toss until fully cooked and evenly coated. Taste, finish with pepper and serve hot.
bo-xao-dau-que.media_alt_text: Beef stir-fried with green beans and garlic on a white ceramic plate.
